The analysis suggests that while AI investment continues, higher borrowing costs and slowing earnings growth could pressure firms to justify their spending on infrastructure.
items.title: Jefferies warns rising borrowing costs threaten global AI expansion

items.summary: Morgan Stanley reports that rapid AI infrastructure investment may outpace electricity availability, creating a power shortfall for US data centers. The firm estimates a 32-gigawatt deficit by 2028, potentially squeezing out smaller competitors. While major tech firms could capture most capacity additions, the lack of power and suitable land may constrain chip deployment and slow the AI boom.
items.title: Morgan Stanley Warns AI Power Shortfall Risks Outpacing Chip Supply

items.summary: US President Donald Trump waived punitive tariffs on countries buying Russian oil, offering India relief from potential 100% duties on US exports. However, experts warn Washington retains the option to revive penalties as leverage in trade negotiations. While India prioritizes energy security, the waiver provides no lasting certainty, leaving New Delhi exposed to renewed US pressure unless it demonstrates that coercion carries a cost.
items.title: Trump Waives Russian Oil Tariffs for India Amid Uncertainty

items.summary: Croatian President Zoran Milanovic met with visiting Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi in Zagreb on October 16, 2026. During the discussion, Milanovic expressed Croatia's willingness to strengthen exchanges and advance mutually beneficial cooperation with China, reaffirming Croatia's commitment to the one-China policy. Wang Yi conveyed greetings from President Xi Jinping and highlighted China's commitment to peaceful development and mutual benefits. The two sides also discussed China-Europe relations, with Wang noting the absence of fundamental conflicts of interest between China and the EU. Milanovic, as an EU member, emphasized maintaining Croatia's independence while adhering to the bloc's common foreign and security policy.
items.title: Croatian President Meets Chinese Foreign Minister to Strengthen Bilateral Cooperation

items.summary: Chinese Vice Premier Ding Xuexiang addressed the 2026 World Vocational and Technical Education Development Conference in Tianjin, calling for strengthened international cooperation in vocational education. He emphasized enhancing policy communication, aligning rules, and promoting cross-border skills allocation. Ding highlighted China's role in global skills training and the need to integrate new technologies into vocational education to meet economic demands.
items.title: Chinese Vice Premier Ding Xuexiang Urges Global Vocational Education Cooperation

items.summary: Volodymyr Zelenskyy warned that Donald Trump's decision to pause sanctions on Russia would intensify the war in Ukraine. He stated that lifting pressure and providing financial rewards encourages Vladimir Putin to continue attacks. This follows a massive Russian strike on Ukraine's energy infrastructure, which Zelenskyy described as one of the worst yet. Zelenskyy called for Europe to negotiate directly with Moscow and urged the US to resurrect the Lindsey Graham sanctions bill. Meanwhile, Trump announced a hold on new sanctions and a deal to purchase Russian diesel, actions Zelenskyy criticized as ignoring the law meant to pressure Russia.
items.title: Zelenskyy Warns Trump Sanctions Lift Will Intensify Ukraine War

items.summary: Former Punjab Chief Minister Sukhbir Badal directly blamed current Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann for the murder of anti-drug activist Parvinder Singh Jhota. Speaking at the SAD office in Chandigarh, Badal accused the AAP-led government of failing to curb drug trafficking and maintain law and order. Badal's wife, Harsimrat Kaur Badal, joined the criticism, alleging a nexus between traffickers and officials and demanding the government's dismissal. The family and protesters are demanding a CBI probe and Mann's resignation.
items.title: Sukhbir Badal Blames Bhagwant Mann for Parvinder Jhota's Murder

items.summary: The India Meteorological Department issued orange alerts for five Kerala districts and yellow alerts for nine others due to heavy rainfall and thunderstorms. The Kerala State Disaster Management Authority urged residents in vulnerable areas to relocate to safer places and avoid water bodies. District control rooms remain operational round the clock, and toll-free numbers are available for assistance.
items.title: Kerala districts under orange and yellow rain alerts

items.summary: A political confrontation in Delhi involves allegations of vote theft and calls for regime change. Janata Party founder Abhijeet Dipke secured conditional bail after signing a 50,000 rupee peace bond, while associates remain jailed. The Congress party received approval to hold a rally at Ramlila Maidan on 1 November. Meanwhile, the opposition challenges Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar in the Supreme Court regarding voter list revisions. Union ministers accuse the opposition of destabilizing the government through street violence, which the Congress denies. The India Today Group also launched an AI-powered Ramayana micro-drama series on its platform Life Tak.
items.title: Political Showdown in Delhi Over Election Commissioner and Vote Theft Allegations

items.summary: Actor Imran Khan Pal filed a petition in the Bombay High Court to challenge a 'leave India' notice issued by the Foreigners Regional Registration Officer. Khan argues the notice is arbitrary, unreasoned, and violates his fundamental rights under Articles 14 and 21 of the Indian Constitution. He claims the action was punitive and aimed at stifling dissent without due process or a hearing. The petition seeks urgent intervention to stay the notice.
items.title: Actor Imran Khan Challenges 'Leave India' Notice in Bombay High Court

items.summary: The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India issued an improvement notice to AB Hotels Limited, operator of the Radisson Blu Hotel in New Delhi, citing food safety lapses. Inspections revealed pest infestations, equipment failures, and improper food handling. Notably, cooking oils with TPC values of 31 and 24.4 were found, exceeding the permitted 25% limit. The regulator directed immediate corrective measures and threatened licence suspension for non-compliance.
items.title: FSSAI Issues Improvement Notice to Radisson Blu Delhi Over Food Safety Violations

items.summary: CNA reported that most haze shelters across Singapore remained empty or locked on Saturday, despite high heat and pollution. While few residents utilized the facilities, those who did, such as retirees Ms Poh and Mr Low, welcomed the air-conditioned respite. Ms Florence Ong also appreciated the free facility, noting it offered relief without needing to run home air-conditioners. The government had recently stepped up measures after PM2.5 readings hit very high levels.
items.title: Few Singaporeans Use Haze Shelters Despite Heat and Pollution

items.summary: A Supreme Court-appointed five-member committee launched a portal to receive complaints regarding violence at Jantar Mantar and other Delhi locations during July 2026. The Union Home Ministry stated the committee will prioritize cases involving pellet guns, harassment of female protesters, and excessive force. Submissions can be made online, in person, or via email to ensure witness protection.
items.title: SC Panel Launches Portal for July Violence Complaints

items.summary: Chilean-American author Isabel Allende won Spain's €1m Premio Planeta literary prize under the pseudonym Luz Ventura. The award, the 75th edition, recognized her sequel to The House of the Spirits, titled La hora antes del alba. Speaking at the ceremony in Barcelona, Allende compared the win to receiving the Nobel Prize. She noted that while the prize is lucrative, it is not the most prestigious in the Spanish-speaking world. The article highlights the prize's history of favoring established writers and mentions a previous instance where a pseudonym was used to conceal three male authors. Allende, 84, stated she entered to avoid the embarrassment of coming last.
items.title: Isabel Allende Wins Spanish Literary Prize Under Pseudonym

items.summary: DMK leader M K Stalin labeled the ruling TVK a "Breaking Bad Party" following the arrest of functionary Boopalan, who officials say concealed 135 kg of methamphetamine. Stalin, citing preliminary investigations, urged authorities to identify others in the alleged narcotics network and dismantle it, questioning how a party member could be involved in such a large-scale operation while publicly advocating against drugs.
items.title: Stalin Calls TVK a Breaking Bad Party After Meth Seizure

items.summary: Sebastian Rucci, a developer with a controversial past, sought to build California's largest AI datacenter in Imperial County, aiming to house Google's AI training. Despite securing interest from Google and promising jobs and tax revenue, the project faced intense local opposition. Residents cited concerns over water scarcity, environmental damage, and noise. Following a judge's ruling requiring an extensive environmental review, construction is paused. Rucci plans to challenge the decision, while the community continues to fight the development.
items.title: Developer's AI Datacenter Project Halted by Community Resistance and Legal Challenges

items.summary: Wasted energy from 50 million electric motors in U.S. factories and buildings could free gigawatts of grid power. Currently, only 16% of industrial and 4% of commercial motors use variable frequency drives (VFDs) to optimize efficiency. Experts argue that wider adoption could supply power for five years of data center growth without new generation. Manufacturers and advocates urge federal agencies and utilities to offer incentives and standards to accelerate rollout, citing rising electricity costs and grid stress as key drivers.
items.title: Wasted Motor Energy Offers Grid Relief Through Variable Frequency Drives

items.summary: ZDNET reports that ten states have legalized plug-in solar systems, allowing residents to install backyard solar setups. While Utah was the first, nine others have followed. Approximately 24 additional states are working on legislation, with some bills advancing in Massachusetts and New York. However, plug-in solar remains illegal in several states due to safety concerns and utility regulations.
items.title: Ten States Legalize Plug-in Solar Systems While Others Advance Legislation

items.summary: Historical ship fires linked to untreated fishmeal led to the adoption of ethoxyquin as a fire retardant in animal feed. While effective in preventing spontaneous combustion, ethoxyquin is now recognized as a carcinogen. Consequently, the European Union and several other nations have banned or restricted its use in animal feed. Despite these restrictions, the chemical remains permitted in the U.S., Australia, Japan, and South Korea. The aquaculture industry continues to face challenges regarding chemical safety and consumer perception, with some companies shifting to alternatives like rosemary extract or vitamin E.
items.title: Ethoxyquin: From Fire Retardant to Controversial Feed Additive

items.summary: A report by Action Against Hunger identifies Pakistan and Bangladesh among the ten nations facing the world's most severe food crises. The study estimates 10.6 million people in Pakistan will need aid in 2026. Globally, 177 million people live in these ten countries, where acute hunger affects 266 million across 47 nations. Pakistan ranked 106th in the 2026 Global Hunger Index with a score of 25.5, categorized as 'serious'. Factors include poverty, climate disasters, and economic instability.
items.title: Pakistan and Bangladesh Rank Among Worst Hunger Nations

items.summary: Pope Leo XIV is set to be discharged from Rome's Gemelli Hospital on Saturday, four days after surgery to remove a lung cancerous growth. The Vatican confirmed he will celebrate Mass and give the Angelus prayer in St Peter's Square on Sunday. Further tests regarding cancer spread are pending, and his fitness for a planned trip to Peru remains unclear.
items.title: Pope Leo XIV Discharged After Lung Cancer Surgery

items.summary: Frontline health workers in Beni, Democratic Republic of Congo, received the Ervebo vaccine on Friday. Health authorities suggest it may offer protection against the related Bundibugyo virus, though efficacy is still being studied. The vaccine is used under a compassionate-use programme. As of Wednesday, the Health Ministry reported 9,066 confirmed cases and 4,381 deaths. The World Health Organization states the outbreak remains out of control.
items.title: Frontline workers in DRC receive Ervebo vaccine amid growing Ebola outbreak

items.summary: Andrew Bailey, the Bank of England governor, participated in a walkout by finance leaders at an IMF meeting in Bangkok. The group departed in protest after Russian finance minister Anton Siluanov addressed them in Russian. Joachim Nagel of the German Bundesbank noted that nearly half the delegates left. European diplomats stated the Ukraine war is existential for Europe and that normalizing relations with Russia is impossible.
items.title: Bank of England Governor Joins IMF Walkout Over Russia

items.summary: A Chinese nursery owner and five staff members were jailed after poisoning over 200 children with lead-tainted food. Li Huifang received a life sentence, while others faced prison terms and fines. Investigations revealed inedible paint was used to enhance meals, resulting in lead levels 2,000 times the safety limit. Dozens of officials were later found attempting to cover up the incident.
items.title: Chinese Nursery Owner Jailed for Life Over Lead Poisoning

items.summary: A Delhi court ordered the release of Cockroach Janta Party founder Abhijeet Dipke on Saturday, a day after his preventive arrest. Police cited traffic concerns and prior violations as reasons for the initial detention. Dipke was released from Mandir Marg police station. Meanwhile, student leader Neha Bora was also released. The arrests occurred amidst protests demanding the resignation of Election Commission chief Kumar over concerns regarding electoral roll revisions.
items.title: Delhi Court Orders Release of Abhijeet Dipke Following Preventive Arrest

items.summary: Hungarian Prime Minister Péter Magyar stated that Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy is unlikely to visit Budapest later this month despite an invitation for the 70th anniversary of the 1956 Hungarian Revolution. Magyar expressed this view in an interview with 444.hu, noting that attendance was improbable even though Russian President Vladimir Putin was not invited. The two leaders previously agreed to meet again later this year at the EU summit in Brussels.
items.title: Hungarian PM Says Zelenskyy Unlikely to Visit Budapest

items.summary: Rolls-Royce is expanding its Goodwood factory with a £300m investment from owner BMW to meet growing demand for highly customised vehicles. The company reports that the average buyer is now 43, down from 56 in 2010, driven by younger, tech-rich clients. Bespoke requests range from interior feathers to dog portraits, with prices reaching seven-figure sums. While production output peaked at 6,032 cars, recent deliveries have fallen. The expansion aims to handle complex commissions rather than increase volume, as the brand navigates challenges like Chinese market slowdowns and a shift in electric vehicle strategy.
items.title: Rolls-Royce Expands Goodwood Factory Amid Custom Craze

items.summary: A list of six new fiction novels is presented, with all information sourced from publishers. The titles include 'Exit Party' by Emily St John Mandel, set in 2031; 'Partita' by Barbara Kingsolver; 'All Our Noble Selves' by Kate Atkinson, set in 1951; 'Victorious' by VE Schwab; 'The Need' by Megan Mostyn Brown; and 'Fair Ones' by Lydia Millet. Brief synopses describe the plots, characters, and settings of each book, ranging from dystopian futures and historical mysteries to supernatural thrillers and family dramas. Specific details, such as character ages and historical dates, are included within the descriptions.
items.title: Six New Novels by Barbara Kingsolver, Kate Atkinson, and Others

items.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy stated that Russia is intensifying attacks on energy infrastructure to cause a blackout before winter. He claimed over 15 critical facilities were targeted and that Moscow aims to leave millions without power. While the Russian Defense Ministry confirmed strikes on specific sites, Zelenskyy also criticized a US sanctions waiver, arguing it encourages further aggression.
items.title: Zelenskyy Accuses Russia of Planned Winter Blackout in Ukraine

items.summary: Senior Labour figures are increasingly worried about the dangers of artificial intelligence, fearing the technology could fall into the hands of bad actors or be used to create bioweapons. While some, like Ed Miliband, warn of threats to humanity, others, such as Prof Elena Simperl, argue that immediate risks like hacking and addiction are more credible than existential threats. The government is currently balancing the need for safety regulations with the desire to avoid falling behind in productivity. Recent warnings from security services and a shift in government posture under Andy Burnham have intensified the focus on AI security and international cooperation.
items.title: Senior Labour Figures Express Deep Concerns Over AI Risks and Safety

items.summary: A doctor at YCM Hospital in Pimpri-Chinchwad was suspended after a viral video allegedly showed a liquor party inside the post-mortem room. PCMC officials ordered an inquiry following the incident involving Dr Vaibhav Avinash Mhaske, who was found intoxicated. Additional Commissioner Kuldeep Jangam issued notices for written explanations, while Municipal Commissioner Vijay Suryavanshi ordered immediate suspension. A departmental inquiry is underway, with a chargesheet anticipated within 15 days.
items.title: Doctor Suspended After Viral Video Shows Liquor in Mortuary

items.summary: Mahela Jayawardene has ended his second stint as head coach of Mumbai Indians, with the franchise confirming his departure. Owner Nita Ambani praised his leadership and contribution, while Jayawardene expressed gratitude for his time with the team. The franchise must now find a new head coach before the November 15 IPL retention deadline.
items.title: Mahela Jayawardene Steps Down as Mumbai Indians Head Coach

items.summary: Abhijeet Dipke, founder of the Cockroach Janta Party, was granted conditional bail by a Special Executive Magistrate court following his detention ahead of a proposed 'Lehra Do Tiranga' march in Delhi. He signed a personal bond of Rs 50,000 and was released immediately. Dipke was arrested under Sections 126 and 170 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita for breach of peace. Other CJP leaders and AISA president Neha Bora were also detained and released after furnishing bonds.
items.title: CJP Founder Abhijeet Dipke Granted Conditional Bail After Detention

items.summary: Decades after apartheid, South Africans are pursuing legal action for past crimes, focusing on the 1960 Sharpeville massacre where police killed at least 69 protesters. Paulina Mathinye, a survivor's descendant, joined a potential class action lawsuit to challenge the Indemnity Act 61 of 1961, which blocks legal redress. The case aims to secure reparations and recognition. Similar efforts include court rulings on the deaths of Chief Albert Luthuli and the Cradock Four, and a reopened inquiry into Steve Biko's death. A formal inquiry is also investigating whether apartheid-era prosecution recommendations were deliberately shelved. These legal moves represent a new wave of efforts to confront historical injustice.
items.title: South Africans Seek Justice for Apartheid-Era Crimes

items.summary: ixigo reported a net profit of Rs 63 crore for Q2 FY27, marking a turnaround from a Rs 3.46 crore loss the prior year. Hotels emerged as the fastest-growing segment with a gross transaction value of Rs 111.34 crore, up 159% year-on-year. Revenue from operations rose to Rs 320.96 crore, supported by a partial stake sale in Freshbus.
items.title: ixigo Reports Q2 Profit Driven by Hotel Booking Growth

items.summary: ICICI Bank reported a 17.7% year-on-year increase in net interest income to Rs 25,339 crore in the second quarter of FY27. The lender's net interest margin stood at 4.18%, while gross non-performing assets declined to 1.20%. Total period-end deposits grew 27.1% to Rs 20.49 lakh crore, and total assets rose 22.6% to Rs 32.93 lakh crore as of September 30, 2026, according to a regulatory filing.
items.title: ICICI Bank Reports Strong Q2 Profit and Asset Growth

items.summary: Iran's Revolutionary Guard Corps stated that a super tanker caught fire after striking a sea mine in the Strait of Hormuz. The IRGC navy accused the vessel of turning off its systems to evade detection while attempting to use an unauthorized route. The US military disputes IRGC control of the strait, asserting it remains open for business.
items.title: IRGC Accuses Tanker of Evading Detection After Mine Strike in Strait of Hormuz

items.summary: The article suggests that book covers often influence selection decisions before a reader can assess the content. To address this, the free app Uncovered.ink is recommended as an alternative to Kindle. This tool allows users to preview the opening chapter of a book directly, bypassing visual marketing and helping readers discover new titles based on the actual text rather than superficial design elements.
items.title: Uncovered.ink Helps Readers Find Books Without Cover Art

items.summary: Europe's solar and storage industry reached nearly one million jobs in 2025, yet Women in Solar+ Europe highlights a retention crisis. While purpose drives recruitment, women leave due to workplace experiences, lack of career progression, and the 'motherhood penalty.' Surveys of 22 European countries indicate nearly four in ten respondents may seek new roles within a year. Experts argue that inspiration alone is insufficient; organizations must implement transparent promotion criteria, flexible policies, and strong leadership to retain talent. The industry faces a competitiveness issue if it fails to support the women who have already committed to the energy transition.
items.title: Solar Industry Faces Retention Challenges Despite Strong Recruitment

items.summary: Groundwater cleanup at the Escambia Wood Treating Company site in Pensacola, Florida, nicknamed Mount Dioxin, is set to begin this fall. The EPA and Escambia County have hired a contractor to treat the contamination, a project estimated to take three to five years. This cleanup follows the 2010 completion of soil remediation and the 1997 relocation of approximately 400 households from the area. The site, originally designated a Superfund site in 1989, remains vacant while awaiting a paying tenant. Future reviews are scheduled for fall 2027.
items.title: Groundwater Cleanup Begins at Florida Superfund Site Decades Later

items.summary: The French government announced measures to accelerate electrification and improve electricity demand flexibility. It plans to exempt solar-plus-storage projects up to 25 MW from current connection limits by the end of 2026, provided grid injection remains under 17 MW. The government also intends to make heat pump subsidies conditional on smart controls from 2027 and encourage smart meter integration. Industry players like Gimelec, EDF, Neoen, and NW Group have committed to expanding flexibility capacity and deploying remote-control systems by 2030, aiming to mobilize gigawatts of capacity and save households money through optimized energy consumption.
items.title: France Eases Grid Rules for Solar-Plus-Storage Projects

items.summary: Hundreds gathered in Melbourne to honor Jayda Allen Bonner, a 21-year-old Indigenous woman killed in an inner-suburban apartment. Her mother and aunt called for action against violence against women. A 31-year-old man was charged with murder. Police investigations continue, with the Homicide Squad examining interactions between police and the victim. Family supporters marched to Parliament demanding domestic violence reforms.
items.title: Hundreds mourn Indigenous woman killed in Melbourne apartment

items.summary: This article presents ten facts regarding the origins of Halloween, tracing the holiday from ancient Celtic rituals to modern American customs. It clarifies that Halloween descends from the Celtic festival of Samhain, which marked the end of harvest and the start of winter roughly 2,000 years ago. The text explains that while Christian holy days and later marketing layers were added, the core seasonal frame remained. Specific traditions like jack-o'-lanterns originated from Irish turnip carvings rather than American pumpkins, and trick-or-treating merged medieval souling with Scottish guising and American pranking in the 1920s and 1930s. The article also notes that associations with Satanism are modern constructs and that the holiday's current candy-centric nature emerged only after World War II.
items.title: Article Debunks Common Halloween Myths and Traces Origins

items.summary: Police in Sydney's Northern Beaches have arrested a 13-year-old boy following multiple reports of alleged sexual touching of women on walking trails around Narrabeen Lagoon. The incidents, occurring between October 1 and 12, involved a man allegedly approaching victims on an e-bike. Superintendent John Duncan stated that police have increased surveillance and patrols while encouraging the public to come forward with information.
items.title: Police Arrest Teenager in Sexual Touching Probe at Narrabeen Lagoon

items.summary: Hundreds of former fighters in Ethiopia's Tigray region have registered for a reintegration program to return to civilian life. They gathered at the Tigray Martyrs' Memorial Monument in Mekelle, two weeks after federal forces recaptured the city. This follows renewed fighting that shattered the 2022 peace agreement. A new caretaker administration has been announced to restore services and prepare for elections.
items.title: Former Tigray Fighters Register for Reintegration Program

items.summary: Japanese Minister Yasuhiro Hanashi announced a government initiative to raise youth awareness regarding the Northern Territories dispute. The plan involves organizing school trips near the islands and sharing information on social media. Hanashi also emphasized promoting the issue abroad and resuming bilateral exchange programs. He described the dispute as the biggest pending issue between Japan and Russia, stating that resolving it is essential for the entire nation.
items.title: Japan Minister Plans Youth Awareness Campaign on Northern Territories Dispute

items.summary: This article presents 15 facts detailing the origins and evolution of Halloween traditions in the United States. It explains that the jack-o'-lantern began as a carved turnip in Ireland and Scotland before pumpkins replaced them due to availability in North America. The text notes that trick-or-treating is a relatively recent custom, emerging in the 1930s and gaining popularity after World War II. Candy corn, originally sold as chicken feed in the 1880s, later became associated with the holiday. The article also covers the history of UNICEF's fundraising campaign, which started in 1950, and discusses the agricultural and retail aspects of pumpkin production and candy sales. It addresses common myths, such as the rarity of a full moon on Halloween and the lack of evidence for poisoned candy scares, attributing the latter to a single family crime in 1974 that fueled broader fears. The piece concludes by comparing Halloween to similar celebrations in other countries and noting its significant impact on the retail calendar.
items.title: Article details 15 facts explaining Halloween traditions and origins

items.summary: Rahul Anand, an IMF official, welcomed Japan's plan to temporarily lower the consumption tax on food to 1% from 8% to address soaring prices. While supporting the targeted, budget-neutral approach, Anand warned against fiscal deterioration given Japan's exceptionally high debt level. He also noted concerns regarding rising long-term interest rates and the need to build buffers while maintaining a downward trend in the debt-to-GDP ratio.
items.title: IMF Official Welcomes Japan's Temporary Tax Cut Plan Amid High Debt Concerns

items.summary: Under-30s describe a bleak lack of nightlife, citing the disappearance of traditional nightclubs in towns like Woking and Tonbridge. The Night Time Industries Association states a quarter of UK towns have lost all nightclubs. Factors include the cost of living crisis and a cultural shift toward sober socialising. Some young people are creating their own events to fill the gap.
items.title: Young people report loss of nightlife venues in UK towns

items.summary: Multilateral development banks published a framework on Saturday to strengthen support for mineral-rich developing economies. The initiative moves beyond extraction to promote processing, refining, and manufacturing. Banks like the World Bank and Asian Development Bank will coordinate financing and infrastructure to boost domestic value addition and attract private investment.
items.title: MDBs Outline Framework to Boost Critical Minerals Processing in Developing Economies

items.summary: Billy Childish, a 66-year-old British punk icon known as Steve Hamper, rejects the commercialization of art, stating that 'Professional art kills art.' He has released over 100 albums and created thousands of paintings since the 1970s. Childish, who grew up in Chatham, works across punk, garage, and folk styles with bands like Thee Headcoats. He refuses to sign contracts, citing a desire for creative freedom. His recent biography by Ted Kessler highlights his authentic, DIY approach. Childish continues to perform and create, emphasizing instinct and personal expression over market demands.
items.title: Billy Childish Rejects Commercial Art in Punk Legacy

items.summary: Thomas Piketty and 44 co-authors from the Global Justice Project propose a future where global wealth shifts from the top 0.001% to the poorest 50%, driven by climate action and sufficiency. While acknowledging the path is politically difficult, Piketty argues that current inequality and climate change create a dystopian alternative. He suggests that without democratic deliberation on issues like shorter working hours and reduced consumption, society risks collapse. The proposal emphasizes international cooperation to avoid resource conflicts and ensure shared prosperity.
items.title: Thomas Piketty Warns of Dystopian Future Prepared by Billionaires

items.summary: Indian Captain Smit Machchhar recounted a harrowing ordeal aboard a flydubai flight in September, where he was allegedly attacked by his Omani co-pilot, Hamam al-Hammami. Machchhar stated he realized he had to act to survive, eventually opening the cockpit door for passengers to intervene. The aircraft diverted to Tabuk after a sharp altitude drop, landing safely.
items.title: Indian Pilot Recalls Near-Death Cockpit Assault Experience

items.summary: Lawyer Ratul Bora plans to challenge two bail orders granted by the Gauhati High Court in the Zubeen Garg death case. Bora alleges loopholes in the charge sheet are weakening the prosecution. While the Singapore Police concluded Garg drowned due to intoxication, Assam authorities maintain it was murder. Bora seeks Supreme Court intervention to prevent further bail grants for the remaining accused.
items.title: Lawyer Challenges Bail Orders in Zubeen Garg Death Case at Supreme Court

items.summary: Portugal is hosting major demonstrations as part of a wider European cost-of-living crisis. Housing rights movements and trade unions affiliated with the CGTP union federation are rallying in Porto, Coimbra, and Lisbon. Protesters cite rising prices, fuel costs, and housing shortages as drivers. While organizers emphasize peaceful assembly, French demonstrations turned violent. Authorities urge protests remain lawful.
items.title: Portugal Joins European Cost-of-Living Protests Amid Housing Crisis

items.summary: Tamil Nadu aims to recover from a disappointing start to their Ranji Trophy campaign with a home match against Uttarakhand at Chepauk in Chennai. Following a loss to Rajasthan where they scored 274 all out after reaching 203 for four, the team utilized time in Chennai to bond and prepare. Coach Yo Mahesh highlighted positives, including a promising bowling unit where debutant Deepesh Devendran took three wickets. However, rain threatens the match, and two players, Washington Sundar and Sai Sudharsan, are unavailable for national duty. Mahesh emphasized the need for ruthless conversion of starts and patience with the bowling department as they adapt to first-class demands.
items.title: Tamil Nadu seeks home comfort to recover from Ranji Trophy setback

items.summary: Pope Leo has been discharged from Gemelli hospital in Rome following surgery to remove a cancerous lung tumour. Doctors stated he was deemed fit for discharge based on clinical tests. Although he walked unaided, uncertainty remains regarding whether the cancer has spread. His upcoming trip to South America may require rescheduling depending on his health recovery.
items.title: Pope Leo Discharged from Hospital After Lung Cancer Surgery

items.summary: The Delhi Traffic Police announced traffic restrictions in CR Park, Greater Kailash-II, and nearby South Delhi areas from October 16 to 20 due to expected large crowds for Durga Puja. Private vehicles will not be allowed to enter these zones between 4 pm and midnight. Authorities recommend using the Delhi Metro and warned against illegal parking to manage congestion on major roads and narrow residential streets.
items.title: Delhi Traffic Police Announces Restrictions for Durga Puja Celebrations

items.summary: Actor Imran Khan challenged a Mumbai Police order directing him to leave India by October 28, citing alleged violations of rules for participating in a political demonstration. He filed a petition in the Bombay High Court seeking to quash the notice, arguing it was issued without inquiry or statutory basis under the Immigration and Foreigners Act. The case tests whether an OCI cardholder can face removal for joining a peaceful protest.
items.title: Imran Khan Challenges Mumbai Police Order to Leave India

items.summary: Ms Zarina Jaffar, a 58-year-old retiree, founded the Facebook group 3R Recycle Sharing is Caring in 2012 to help others after losing her husband in a 2008 accident. The initiative, which has 14 administrators and volunteers, provides aid ranging from groceries to utility bills. Jaffar emphasizes that help should be temporary to encourage self-reliance, though she has faced criticism for assisting some families. She also advocates for her son, who faced employment barriers due to a past offence. Jaffar, who received an Exemplary Mother Award in 2025, balances her charity work with her role as a mother, acknowledging periods of neglect but remaining committed to her mission.
items.title: Ms Zarina Jaffar founded a charity group after losing her husband

items.summary: Actor Imran Khan challenged a Mumbai Police notice ordering him to leave India by October 28 for participating in a political demonstration. Filed through his advocate, the plea argued the notice was illegal and lacked statutory basis, as OCI cardholders can protest peacefully. The Bombay High Court is set to hear the matter urgently.
items.title: Imran Khan Challenges Illegal Leave India Notice in Court

items.summary: Senegal's former president Macky Sall announced his withdrawal from the race to lead the United Nations. He stated he hoped to contribute to a consensus candidate. This decision follows a recent informal poll where all seven candidates received at least one veto from permanent Security Council members. While none of the polls are binding, Sall's exit leaves Uganda's Olara Otunnu as the only African contender for the position.
items.title: Senegal's Macky Sall Withdraws from UN Secretary-General Race

items.summary: At a World Bank meeting in Bangkok, Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman urged the use of knowledge resources to study market failures in urbanisation, tourism, agricultural exports, and critical minerals. She emphasized that developing economies lack risk capital, which hinders job creation. While acknowledging her role as India's Finance Minister, the article notes her remarks reflect a focus on inclusive growth and poverty alleviation, contrasting with the government's rhetoric of India as a top five economy. The piece suggests that despite India's desire to be seen as an emerging power, it faces significant challenges typical of a developing economy, including a large poor population and the need for resilient economic policies.
items.title: Finance Minister Sitharaman highlights market failures and job concerns at World Bank meeting

items.summary: The Indian Embassy in Bucharest confirmed that all nine Indian seafarers aboard the chemical tanker YARA J are safe after the vessel reached the Port of Constanta. The Ambassador verified their status following consultations with Romanian authorities and the ship's security officer. Meanwhile, three other Indian nationals rescued from a different vessel have already departed Romania.
items.title: Indian Embassy Confirms Safety of Seafarers on Chemical Tanker in Romania

items.summary: The article presents a collection of opinionated observations regarding technology, social behavior, and current events. The author argues that new technologies are immediately misused to harass women, citing examples like smartglasses and AI-generated deepfakes. A specific incident in Cologne involving a humanoid robot is mentioned as police investigate. The piece also touches on various unrelated topics, including a school's halted robot plan, predictions about future robot adoption, legal cases involving a man accused of rape, and political commentary on figures like Katie Miller and Sally Rooney. The text concludes with a sarcastic remark about wildlife photography.
items.title: Op-Ed Criticizes Tech Harassment and Social Trends

items.summary: Delhi Police granted a No Objection Certificate to the Congress party for a protest rally at Ramlila Maidan on November 1 against the SIR policy. This approval followed the denotification of Jantar Mantar as a designated protest site. The police identified Ramlila Maidan, Burari Ground, and CBD Ground as alternative venues. Rohit Rajbar, DCP Central Delhi Police, confirmed the process after the party secured venue availability from the Municipal Corporation of Delhi.
items.title: Delhi Police approves Congress rally at Ramlila Maidan for SIR protest

items.summary: ConnectWise shut down access to its Cloud Backup service after hackers compromised Microsoft 365 tenants. Huntress confirmed at least 162 compromised tenants in its environment, while Microsoft identified unauthorized authentication attempts from a single IP address on October 15. Researchers from Todyl noted the attacker used the backup application's secret to gain permissions, allowing access to emails and files. ConnectWise stated it has no evidence that partner backup data was compromised, though existing archives remain inaccessible until services are restored. The company is investigating and engaged in remediation efforts.
items.title: Hackers Breach Microsoft 365 Tenants via ConnectWise Supply-Chain Attack

items.summary: Elon Musk and his America Pac political action committee agreed to settle two class action lawsuits alleging they defrauded voters in closely contested states before the 2024 US election. The plaintiffs claimed Musk promised a $1m daily lottery to petition signatories. While the defendants denied the allegations, a federal judge in Austin, Texas, noted the settlements require court approval. Musk, CEO of Tesla and SpaceX, must testify in the cases.
items.title: Elon Musk Settles Election Lottery Lawsuits Over Alleged Voter Fraud

items.summary: Green Visakha, an environmental NGO, has demanded the cancellation of permissions for Google's proposed $15 billion AI data centre project in Visakhapatnam and Anakapalli districts, Andhra Pradesh. The group, citing concerns over environmental implications and lack of compliance with the Data Centre Evaluation Framework, called for a halt to construction at Tarluvada and Adavivaram. Following a rally marking the first anniversary of the state government's MoU with Google, Green Visakha urged the government to disclose agreement details via a white paper and conduct a public hearing. The organisation also plans to involve mayoral and corporator candidates in the electoral debate regarding the project's sustainability.
items.title: Green Visakha Demands Halt to Google AI Data Centre Project in Vizag

items.summary: Anthropic is privately circulating a draft bill aimed at regulating frontier artificial intelligence safety. The proposal seeks to set a high threshold for federal intervention, requiring that a model pose a foreseeable danger of causing more than $1 billion in damage or killing or severely injuring more than 50 people. Under the plan, only a federal judge could suspend a model, and independent evaluators would assess laboratories. The draft would also override some state-level regulations. This move follows federal officials placing two of Anthropic's advanced models under export controls, which caused concern in Silicon Valley over arbitrary government intervention.
items.title: Anthropic Proposes Bill to Limit Federal AI Model Halts

items.summary: India has announced import duty concessions under its free trade agreement with New Zealand, effective October 20. The Finance Ministry notified zero basic customs duty for sheep meat and a 15% rate for kiwi fruit imports valued at $2.50 per kg or more. Other products like wine and manuka honey also receive preferential rates, while dairy remains excluded.
items.title: India Cuts Tariffs on New Zealand Sheep Meat and Kiwi Fruit

items.summary: Police reported a stampede at the Sarada Park Durga Puja pandal in Kolkata around 7:40 pm on Saturday. Heavy crowds gathered amid rainfall, causing a rush at the exit gate. Officials stated that approximately 35 persons were shifted to MCH for treatment. At least 35 people were injured, with 10 feared dead. West Bengal Governor Ravi expressed grief over the tragic incident.
items.title: Kolkata Pandal Stampede Leaves 10 Feared Dead and 35 Injured Amid Rain

items.summary: Shiv Sena (UBT) chief Uddhav Thackeray supported opposition demands for regime change, arguing that a government restricting voting and protest rights must be replaced. He cited alleged police brutality against youth and women in Delhi. Senior advocate Prashant Bhushan also called for regime change, stating disaffection is not a crime. Conversely, Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis accused the opposition of seeking to topple the government outside democratic processes.
items.title: Shiv Sena Chief Uddhav Thackeray Supports Opposition Call for Regime Change Amid Protests

items.summary: Fu Cong, China's permanent representative to the UN, urged stronger global climate governance and an accelerated green transition during a high-level meeting ahead of COP31. Speaking on September 21, 2026, he emphasized multilateral cooperation, the implementation of the Paris Agreement, and support for developing nations. Fu noted China's engagement with over 100 countries and regions in green cooperation.
items.title: China Calls for Stronger Global Climate Governance at UN Meeting

items.summary: The Jakarta-Bandung High-Speed Railway, known as Whoosh, marked its third anniversary on September 25, 2026, having carried more than 18 million passenger trips. Since its launch, the line has operated 58,666 train services, accumulating over 8. 9 million kilometers of safe operation with a 99. 4% on-time rate. Daily services have increased from 14 to 62 during peak periods, and single-day ridership peaked at 26,770. The railway has also expanded passenger services, with 47,577 frequent traveler cards sold since June 2024. Customer satisfaction stands at 95. 79%, with 98. 27% satisfied with punctuality and 97.
items.title: Whoosh Railway Celebrates Three Years of Operation in Indonesia

items.summary: SBI Research urged the government to provide tax clarity on government securities and clearer rules for external commercial borrowings. The research arm of the State Bank of India stated that these policy measures could deepen domestic borrowing avenues and support capital flows. This recommendation comes amid persistent pressure on India's balance of payments and global financial turbulence.
items.title: SBI Research Calls for Tax Clarity and ECB Rules to Support India's Capital Flows

items.summary: On October 17, CGTN launched the Global South Directors Co-Production Program 2026 to mark the International Day for the Eradication of Poverty. The initiative brings together documentary filmmakers from approximately 20 countries across Asia, Africa, Latin America, and Europe to explore themes of poverty reduction, sustainable development, and social resilience through locally-led storytelling.
items.title: CGTN Launches Global South Directors Co-Production Program 2026

items.summary: Around 300 YSRC families from Srikakulam and Vizianagaram districts joined the Telugu Desam party ahead of local body elections. The inductions included 200 families from Gollaveedhi in Tekkali panchayat and 100 from Vizianagaram district. Agriculture minister Kinjarapu Atchannaidu welcomed the families, while another 100 from East Baliji Veedhi also switched sides. The moves occurred amid political defections in the region.
items.title: Hundreds of YSRC families join Telugu Desam ahead of polls

items.summary: Seven nominations for the mayor and 594 for ward members were filed in Visakhapatnam over two days. Candidates from the YSRC, BSP, BCYP, and as independents submitted papers. Scrutiny begins October 19, with polling scheduled for October 28. Results are expected on October 30.
items.title: Seven Mayor Nominations and 594 Ward Posts Filed in Visakhapatnam

items.summary: The Kerala High Court refused a stay on the reconstitution of the State Waqf Board under M C Mayin Haji. The Kerala government dissolved the previous board, which was headed by K S Hamsa, and appointed a new committee. Hamsa challenged the move, arguing it violated court directions and lacked legal authority. The court rejected the request for a stay, noting no case was made for a stringent interim order. The new board, including members from the IUML, took charge while legal challenges regarding representation and the appointment process continue. Waqf Minister N Samsudheen stated the reconstitution was done to address disputes and protect properties.
items.title: Kerala High Court Rejects Stay on Waqf Board Reconstitution Under Mayin Haji

items.summary: This article examines the Jio Platforms IPO, contextualizing it within the transformative history of India's telecom sector. It details Jio's disruptive 2016 launch, which drastically reduced data costs and reshaped the market landscape, leading to the consolidation of major competitors. The piece analyzes the IPO's pricing and valuation, noting a price band of ₹1,065 to ₹1,119 and a potential market capitalization of 10.3 lakh crore. It compares Jio's metrics, such as an EV/EBITDA of around 14.4 times, against peers like Airtel. While acknowledging Jio's strong growth and market share, the article highlights valuation risks and the potential for margin compression, suggesting the IPO represents an opportunity for investors to gain exposure to a well-managed company with significant potential.
items.title: Jio Platforms IPO Analysis: History, Valuation, and Future Outlook

items.summary: A stampede-like situation occurred at the Chorbagan Durga Puja pandal in Kolkata following sudden heavy rain, causing chaos and a partial structure collapse. Kolkata Police reported around 35 to 40 injuries, with several fatalities. Authorities are investigating crowd management lapses after volunteers were reportedly outnumbered. Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee expressed shock, while police have initiated an inquiry into security failures.
items.title: Stampede at Kolkata Durga Puja Pandal Kills Several, Injures 40

items.summary: Belgium's foreign minister, Maxime Prevot, stated that masked settlers attacked a group of European diplomats in the occupied West Bank on Saturday. At least four people have been killed and more than 100 injured since the harvest began, according to the Palestinian health ministry. Prevot condemned the violence and linked it to Israel's settlement policy, while Israeli authorities called it a severe act of violence.
items.title: Masked Settlers Attack European Diplomats in Occupied West Bank

items.summary: Police stated that at least 25 people were injured during a crowd surge at a Durga Puja pandal in north Kolkata on Saturday evening. A senior officer explained that rain caused the crowd to rush, leading to the incident. West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari and other officials visited the hospital where the injured were being treated. While some news channels reported deaths, there is no official confirmation of the death count.
items.title: Stampede at Kolkata Durga Puja injures 25 people

items.summary: Europe anticipates a challenging winter characterized by rising fuel costs and low gas reserves. The European Union has paid an additional €100 billion on oil and gas this year, with total extra energy costs surpassing €900 billion since 2022. Gas storage has fallen to its lowest level since 2022, standing at around 67 per cent full in September compared to a seasonal average of 80 per cent. Germany is expected to miss its 80 per cent storage target. EU energy commissioner Dan Jorgensen warned of high prices but reassured that no supply issues are expected. Meanwhile, the European Commission calls for reduced consumer demand to manage supplies.
items.title: Europe Faces Winter Energy Crisis Amid Rising Costs and Low Gas Reserves

items.summary: Researchers at the University of Texas at Austin propose using wastewater from the oil and gas industry to cool AI data centers. Their study suggests reverse osmosis or vapor heating could sustainably reduce pressure on freshwater resources. The Permian Basin alone generates roughly 790 million gallons of wastewater daily, far exceeding the 5 million gallons a large data center consumes. This approach aims to close a resource loop while addressing water scarcity.
items.title: Texas Researchers Propose Using Permian Wastewater for AI Data Centers

items.summary: Police stated that at least 35 people were injured in a stampede triggered by a crowd surge at a Durga Puja pandal in north Kolkata. Rain prompted a rush, causing some to fall and triggering chaos. Governor Ravi expressed sorrow, while officials visited injured patients. An eyewitness reported people fainting and being taken on motorcycles. Authorities deployed disaster management teams and closed the site.
items.title: Stampede at Kolkata Durga Puja Pandal Injures 35

items.summary: Chelsea goalkeeper Emi Martinez suffered a concussion during a collision with Everton's Jarrad Branthwaite in a 2-0 Premier League victory. Manager Xabi Alonso stated Martinez required precautionary tests at the hospital. The incident overshadowed Pedro Neto's double, which ended Everton's unbeaten start. Mike Penders made his debut as a replacement.
items.title: Chelsea Goalkeeper Martinez Concussed in Everton Clash

items.summary: A stampede at a Durga Puja pandal in Kolkata left at least 18 people dead and several injured. While official confirmation on the death toll is pending, leaders including PM Modi and West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari visited the injured. The Bengal Governor RN Ravi expressed grief over the loss of lives. Authorities have launched helplines and closed several crowded pandals following the incident.
items.title: Kolkata Stampede Tragedy: 18 Dead, Leaders Mourn

items.summary: India set a new record for their fastest team fifty in men's T20I cricket, reaching 50 runs in just 2.5 overs against the West Indies in Bengaluru. However, persistent rain forced the series decider to be abandoned. The match was reduced to a five-over chase, but the West Indies could not chase down the target, leaving the five-match series level at 2-2.
items.title: Rain washes out India vs West Indies T20I decider

items.summary: The Maharashtra State Common Entrance Test Cell reported that 10,395 students secured MBBS and BDS seats after the third Centralised Admission Process round for the 2026-27 academic year. Approximately 1,036 seats remain vacant out of 11,431 available. Government medical colleges nearly completed admissions with only 20 vacancies remaining, while private institutions and dental colleges have lower occupancy rates. The CET Cell announced revised schedules for three online stray vacancy rounds to fill the remaining positions, with preference submission deadlines set for October 17 and 18.
items.title: Maharashtra Fills Over 10,000 Medical Seats After Third CAP Round

items.summary: Euronews correspondents covering protests in Paris reported being assaulted by masked looters and rioters on Saturday. Estelle Nilsson-Julien described her cameraman being hit and their camera stolen, though the SD card was missing. Another correspondent, Valerie Gauriat, noted a protester slapping her head. The violence followed social media calls to target media personnel to prevent coverage of the demonstrations.
items.title: Euronews Crew Assaulted During Paris Protests

items.summary: Matunga police registered an FIR against Delnaz Anklesaria and others for allegedly forging a court order to mislead the Bombay High Court. The case stems from a marital dispute where the complainant, Eric Jimmy Anklesaria, claimed his wife submitted a fabricated order dated November 15, 2025, during legal proceedings. Verification revealed no such official order existed in court records. The police initiated an investigation under sections of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita.
items.title: Police Register FIR Against Woman For Allegedly Forging Court Order

items.summary: The Supreme Court upheld a Madras High Court ruling denying SC and OBC reservation benefits to those converting from Hinduism. This decision affects Tamil Nadu's quota for Muslim OBCs. Meanwhile, Karnataka and Madhya Pradesh governments plan to challenge High Court rulings that struck down laws raising reservation percentages, citing concerns over exceeding the 50% constitutional cap.
items.title: Supreme Court Upholds Reservation Ruling as States Plan Challenges

items.summary: Protesters stormed Marseille's town hall on Saturday during nationwide demonstrations over rising prices in France, clashing with police as tensions escalated. According to AFP journalists at the scene, demonstrators forced their way through the building's doors, overturned a bust of Marianne, and damaged furniture inside the entrance hall. Police later intervened to clear the building.
items.title: Protesters Clash with Police During Town Hall Storming in Marseille

items.summary: Parashar filed an FIR against Rahul Gandhi alleging he pushed her during an October 12 protest at the Supreme Court. She stated she was three months pregnant at the time and claimed Gandhi's supporters shouted at her instead of helping. Parashar requested police action against Gandhi and others involved, urging media organizations to release footage of the incident.
items.title: Parashar files FIR against Rahul Gandhi over alleged push during protest

items.summary: Nigeria shut down a major illegal gold mining operation in Gashaka-Gumti National Park, displacing more than 4,000 miners, according to the Africa Nature Investors Foundation. While officials call the closure a success, they warn miners may return due to economic pressures. The park, a stronghold for the Nigeria-Cameroon chimpanzee, faces ongoing threats from illegal mining and insecurity. Authorities acknowledge that without addressing root causes like poverty, conservation efforts remain fragile. Former miners report losing livelihoods, though some have found alternative work. The operation highlights the complex challenge of balancing biodiversity protection with community needs in Nigeria's protected areas.
items.title: Nigeria closes illegal gold mine in national park amid conservation and livelihood concerns

items.summary: A stampede occurred outside the Chorbagan Durga Puja pandal in north Kolkata on Saturday evening as rain caused a crowd to rush forward. A senior police officer stated that people fell on the road during the incident. News channels reported 17 deaths, though there is no official confirmation of the death count. West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari visited a state-run hospital where injured individuals were being treated.
items.title: Several Feared Killed in Durga Puja Pandal Stampede in Kolkata

items.summary: Thousands rallied in Lisbon, Porto, and Coimbra on October 17, 2026, demanding higher wages, better pensions, and affordable housing amid rising living costs. The General Confederation of Portuguese Workers organized the demonstrations. A housing movement spokesperson stated mobilization would continue until conditions improved. The Socialist Party leader expressed solidarity and called for clarification regarding a recent police operation that ended a protest encampment in Porto.
items.title: Thousands Rally in Portugal for Higher Wages and Affordable Housing

items.summary: A Saturday roundup links to posts on AI understanding economics, famous state books, and various commentary on Adam Tooze, Susannah Clarke, and Caracas safety.
items.title: Saturday assorted links cover AI, books, and economics

items.summary: Scuffles and fires broke out as protesters rallied across France, joining students in demonstrations against rising living costs. Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez's office reported at least 272 arrests and described growing violent incidents, including assaults on police and damage to public buildings. Authorities deployed tear gas and water cannons in Paris, while similar tensions erupted in Lyon, Marseille, and other cities. The protests, which revived the 'yellow vest' movement, reflect widespread frustration over spiked prices and have influenced the presidential election campaign.
items.title: Violent Protests Erupt Across France Amid Rising Living Costs

items.summary: Assam Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma shared an emotional post celebrating his son Nandil receiving a law degree from NLSIU Bengaluru. Sarma highlighted his son's decision to take a year off for CLAT preparation, noting Nandil secured an All India Rank of 40. During the 34th annual convocation, Chief Justice of India Surya Kant addressed graduates, urging them to uphold justice and defend liberty.
items.title: Assam CM Celebrates Son's Law Degree at NLSIU Convocation

items.summary: Borussia Dortmund secured a goalless draw against Union Berlin in Berlin, keeping them provisionally top of the Bundesliga with 14 points. Striker Konstantinos Karetsas suffered an ankle injury shortly after returning from a previous collapse due to circulatory problems. The result ended Dortmund's winless streak across their last three matches, though they remain without a victory in the Champions League.
items.title: Dortmund Draw Keeps Them Top Despite Karetsas Injury

items.summary: Six US lawmakers, including Pramila Jayapal and Ilhan Omar, urged Secretary of State Marco Rubio to discuss alleged police excesses against Indian protesters with authorities during his October visit. The lawmakers cited reports of wrongful detention and force used during demonstrations demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. Indian officials dismissed the remarks as unwarranted interference in India's democratic processes.
items.title: US Lawmakers Urge Rubio to Address Indian Police Excesses

items.summary: Artist Joe Namy has installed 'Cosmic Breath,' a multi-channel sound installation in central London, featuring recordings of the Islamic call to prayer (adhan). The work, displayed at Ibraaz's Musalla, juxtaposes historical and contemporary calls from various global locations to create a sonic sanctuary. Namy explains that the installation serves as an antidote to the heightened Islamophobia and xenophobia currently affecting the UK. The piece includes a local recording from Walthamstow made during the 2020 pandemic and traces its conceptual roots to a 2020 protest in Durban where residents broadcast the adhan via car speakers to defy a ban. By amplifying these diverse auditory traditions, the artwork aims to foster connection and challenge hostility within the community.
items.title: Artist Joe Namy Installs Cosmic Breath in London to Counter Islamophobia

items.summary: Pope Leo XIV left Rome's Gemelli Hospital days after surgery to remove part of his right lung. Doctors confirmed his condition allowed discharge, noting he is expected to lead prayers soon. The procedure addressed a lung adenocarcinoma diagnosis. While recovery is estimated at about one week, the Pope's schedule remains cleared through October 20, with upcoming international travel planned.
items.title: Pope Leo XIV Discharged After Lung Cancer Surgery

items.summary: An article argues that Britain should reject cheap Chinese artificial intelligence due to significant security and political risks. It highlights that Chinese models, such as those from DeepSeek and Xiaomi, allow users to access core software without expensive licenses, but this comes with embedded political censorship and data privacy concerns. Experts like Ross Burley and Michael Wooldridge warn that hosting these models does not remove state control or security weaknesses, as data may be shared with Chinese authorities. The piece suggests that relying on such technology undermines data security and industry stability, recommending instead the adoption of US or domestic alternatives.
items.title: Britain Should Reject Cheap Chinese AI Due to Security Risks

items.summary: The Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC) demolished unauthorised portions of a bungalow in Juhu owned by actor Ajay Devgn and his mother. Officials stated the action followed a stop-work notice regarding alleged illegal alterations. Devgn's office clarified the property is rented out and claimed all rules were followed, while the BMC noted its orders did not explicitly name the actors.
items.title: BMC Demolishes Unauthorised Portions of Ajay Devgn's Juhu Property

items.summary: China has emerged as a major player in the global gaming industry, with over 700 million regular players, despite strict regulations and a former console ban. Developers like Connor Xu are creating unique historical games such as 'The Defiant' and 'Black Myth: Wukong' to appeal to international audiences. The market operates under a licensing system requiring approval from government ministries, prohibiting content that threatens national unity or spreads information disrupting public order. While Western developers must also comply with these rules to access the large Chinese market, experts warn of potential self-censorship affecting creative standards worldwide.
items.title: China's Gaming Industry Grows Despite Strict Regulations

items.summary: Drupal has patched two critical vulnerabilities affecting its core and contributed modules, allowing remote code execution. The security team urges administrators to apply updates immediately, warning that exploits could emerge within hours or days. Specific versions are recommended, while older releases are marked end-of-life. Drupal Steward offers partial protection but does not cover all vectors.
items.title: Drupal Patches Critical Remote Code Execution Flaws

items.summary: Egypt's President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi stated he will leave office when his term expires in 2030, describing the matter as completely settled. Speaking to graduates and officials, he affirmed the constitution would not be touched. The 71-year-old leader, who became president in 2014, plans to use the period to groom new leaders, though critics speculate about potential constitutional changes to extend his tenure.
items.title: Egypt's President Sisi Announces Departure in 2030

items.summary: Protesters clashed with police across France during nationwide rallies focused on education and the cost of living. Demonstrations occurred in cities including Marseille, Lyon, Rennes, and Gueret, with some protesters storming buildings and setting fires. Authorities detained hundreds of people in Paris and nationwide. President Emmanuel Macron called for calm, while political parties from the far-left to the far-right capitalized on the unrest. The protests, which some link to the Yellow Vest movement, take place ahead of the upcoming presidential election. Public concern over inflation and purchasing power remains high.
items.title: French Students Clash with Police Amid Cost of Living Protests

items.summary: The RSPCA's Medway West branch launched a reduced-cost veterinary clinic to assist pet owners on low incomes or receiving benefits. In its first 11 days, the clinic treated 160 pets. Staff noted that rising living costs have left some capable owners unable to care for their animals. The branch also operates a pet food bank supplying thousands of items in 2026.
items.title: RSPCA Opens Low-Cost Clinic to Help Pet Owners in Medway

items.summary: Meta has taken the lead in American open-weight models with the release of Muse Spark Open, which is now considered the strongest domestic open model by a significant margin. This development narrows the performance gap between Western and Chinese models, which previously outnumbered Western counterparts in quality. While Muse Spark Open offers strong capabilities, its adoption may be influenced by a restrictive custom license requiring revenue gating and specific attribution. The article notes that Meta is the only American company currently offering both frontier open and closed models, positioning it uniquely against competitors like Anthropic and OpenAI. The piece highlights Meta's organizational efficiency under Alex Wang as a key factor in its recent success, contrasting it with the bureaucratic challenges faced by other labs.
items.title: Meta Leads US Open-Weight Model Race Amidst Competitive Shift

items.summary: Delhi recorded 211 clean-air days in 2026, the highest since 2016 excluding the pandemic year. Environment Minister Manjinder Singh Sirsa attributed this to government efforts and public cooperation. However, he cautioned that sustaining these gains through the winter season remains a critical challenge requiring strict implementation of pollution-control protocols.
items.title: Delhi Records 211 Clean-Air Days in 2026 Amid Winter Concerns

items.summary: Viral videos claiming YouTuber Dhruv Rathee was arrested by Noida Police have been denied by the Gautam Buddh Nagar Police Commissionerate, which called the reports false and misleading. The police clarified that Rathee was not arrested in Noida. Separately, Rathee alleged he was taken into custody in Gurugram on October 10 and described the incident as kidnapping.
items.title: Police Deny Viral Claim of Dhruv Rathee Arrest

items.summary: An investigation by the environmental watchdog Mighty Earth reveals that US corporate lobbyists conducted a two-year campaign to weaken the EU Deforestation Regulation. The report cites over 350 meetings between major US firms, including Cargill and Bunge, and EU officials between July 2024 and July 2026. While US representatives deny a concerted effort to derail the rules, claiming they raised legitimate implementation concerns, the analysis suggests a strategy to dilute the legislation. The law, set to take effect in December, prohibits imports of commodities linked to deforestation. Mighty Earth calls for greater transparency in lobbying activities to ensure balance.
items.title: Mighty Earth Report Details US Lobbying Against EU Deforestation Law

items.summary: Linda Geddes discovered her name was used by an impersonator to pitch stories and publish articles under her byline. The fraudster, dubbed 'Fake Linda', allegedly used AI tools to create convincing pitches and lifted quotes from Geddes's previous work without attribution. This incident mirrors similar cases involving other journalists and researchers whose identities have been hijacked for financial gain or reputational damage. Geddes, who works in science journalism, found the deception unsettling as it threatens her professional credibility. While the motive remains unclear, experts suggest the use of generative AI and deepfakes is making such impersonations easier. Geddes has reported the matter to authorities and is seeking to identify the perpetrator.
items.title: Journalist Linda Geddes Investigates Impersonation Scam

items.summary: Pope Leo XIV was discharged from Gemelli hospital in Rome four days after doctors removed part of his right lung to treat a cancerous tumour. He is expected to return to the Vatican and resume the Angelus prayer. His planned voyage to South America is uncertain, and he has cancelled audiences until October 20 while awaiting further test results.
items.title: Pope Leo XIV Discharged After Lung Cancer Surgery

items.summary: IDBI Bank reported a 39% year-on-year decline in net profit to Rs 2,205 crore for Q2 FY26, though excluding a Rs 1,699 crore one-off gain from an NSDL sale, profit rose 14%. Net interest income fell 49% to Rs 1,353 crore, while the net NPA ratio improved to 0.17% as of September 30, 2026.
items.title: IDBI Bank Reports Q2 Profit Drop Amid Investment Gain

items.summary: Katie Zacharia departed her role as White House press secretary just five days into the position, following heavy criticism of her brief inaugural briefing. President Donald Trump suggested she leave, stating she did not need the job. Zacharia admitted she had not passed the bar exam, a fact she initially concealed, claiming she was hired for communications, not legal work. Her departure is the quickest among Trump's press team, surpassing the ten-day tenure of Anthony Scaramucci. Democrats have seized on the exit as a sign of failure in the Republican White House ahead of the November midterm elections.
items.title: Katie Zacharia Leaves White House Press Secretary Role After Five Days

items.summary: HDFC Bank reported a 5% year-on-year rise in net profit to Rs 19,510 crore for the quarter ended September 30, 2026. Net interest income grew 9.7% to Rs 34,620 crore, while the bank's total balance sheet expanded to Rs 45.78 lakh crore. Asset quality remained stable with declining non-performing assets, and average advances increased by 14.1% compared to the previous year.
items.title: HDFC Bank Reports Profit Rise and Asset Growth in Q2

items.summary: A carved pumpkin begins deteriorating immediately after cutting, as the rind no longer protects internal moisture from evaporation and microbial invasion. Decay speed varies based on temperature, humidity, and initial preparation. The article outlines ten methods to prolong freshness, including selecting pumpkins with firm stems and unbroken skin, thoroughly scraping interior pulp, and using smaller, cleaner cuts. Post-carving care involves soaking the pumpkin in a diluted bleach solution to kill spores, sealing cut edges with petroleum jelly to slow evaporation, and storing the pumpkin in a cool, shaded location. Daily misting and reapplication of sealant are recommended for extended display. Using battery-operated LED lights instead of candles prevents internal heat damage. Timing the carving close to the display date further reduces the window for decay.
items.title: Simple Tricks to Extend Your Carved Pumpkin's Life

items.summary: Clashes occurred between police and protesters during mass rallies across France on Saturday, driven by concerns over high prices, social inequalities, and the state of the education system. The Interior Ministry reported that approximately 272 people were arrested by mid-afternoon following violent incidents in cities including Paris, Marseilles, Rennes, Toulouse, and Angers. Authorities estimate nearly 200,000 people will attend the demonstrations, though some rallies have been restricted. Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu expressed concern about the atmosphere of perma-crisis, while President Emmanuel Macron called for calm and respect. The protests involve students, trade unionists, and remnants of the Yellow Vests movement.
items.title: Police and protesters clash in nationwide French demonstrations over social issues

items.summary: Researchers at Djillali Liabes University analyzed a 12 MW solar plant in Sidi Bel-Abbes from 2018 to 2023. Their study found that performance declined significantly in 2020 due to reduced maintenance during COVID-19 restrictions. The performance ratio fell to 78.74% that year before recovering to 84.83% in 2023, highlighting the importance of regular upkeep for optimal system performance.
items.title: Algerian Researchers Link Solar Plant Performance Drop to Pandemic Maintenance Cuts

items.summary: Spanish researchers tested low-height photovoltaic systems in three southeastern Spain vineyards during the 2024 harvest. The study, led by scientists from the Polytechnic University of Cartagena and Imida, found that these designs preserve agronomic integrity while generating electricity. Results showed land-use efficiency ratios between 1.16 and 1.53, with one system reaching 1.95. Annual energy production varied by site, ranging from 304,716 to 555,905 kWh per hectare.
items.title: Spanish Researchers Validate Low-Height Agrivoltaics in Vineyards

items.summary: Dang Yangyang, general manager of Wintop Food in Tengzhou, China, describes a surge in international demand for Chinese chicken. Clients from nations including Ghana, Iraq, and Russia seek the product. Wintop processes 60 million chickens annually, with exports accounting for half of its profits. Dang notes that while international clients previously distrusted quality, the price advantage of $1,000 per ton compared to Brazilian and Thai competitors now drives sales.
items.title: Chinese Chicken Export Boom Driven by Price Advantage

items.summary: SoftBank Group is considering acquiring Allied Universal, the largest U.S. security services company, as founder Masayoshi Son explores deploying AI robots. The potential deal could value Allied at up to $18 billion, with total value near $30 billion including $12 billion in debt, according to people familiar with the matter and Bloomberg data.
items.title: SoftBank Group Considers Acquiring U.S. Security Firm Allied Universal

items.summary: In Venezuela, women continue to perform clandestine abortions due to strict laws and economic hardship, often relying on clandestine networks or crossing into Colombia where the procedure is legal. A 2025 survey found 5.1% of 500 women admitted to medication abortions, while poverty affects 80% of female-headed households. Although Colombia allows abortion up to the 24th week, a new president opposes it, and U.S. funding cuts threaten migrant support services. In Venezuela, legal exceptions are practically nonexistent, leaving women defenseless against criminalization and abandonment.
items.title: Venezuelan Women Seek Secret Abortions Amidst Border Threats and Legal Restrictions

items.summary: Journalist Marta Sader argues that the rise of modern mysticism, including horoscopes and tarot, reflects neoliberal individualism rather than contradicting technological advancement. In her book 'Liquid Spirituality,' Sader explains to EL PAÍS that these practices offer peace of mind in an uncertain world by placing responsibility for healing on the individual. She notes that this approach aligns with marketing strategies and can serve as a gateway to dangerous pseudoscience and far-right conspiracy theories. Sader suggests that while these beliefs appeal to privileged, individualistic people, they ultimately mask systemic flaws by framing personal failures as the result of insufficient attention.
items.title: Journalist Marta Sader Links Modern Mysticism to Neoliberal Individualism

items.summary: LPT Skills, an AI-first professional upskilling institute headquartered in Jodhpur, Rajasthan, is restructuring its digital marketing education to address the transformative impact of artificial intelligence on the industry. The institute emphasizes integrating emerging technologies with established marketing principles, focusing on practical training, live projects, and specialized courses in AI SEO and Generative Engine Optimization. With a maximum batch size of 30 students, LPT Skills aims to bridge the gap between theoretical knowledge and workplace readiness. By offering both offline and online formats, the institute seeks to make specialized training accessible to learners across India, preparing them for evolving roles that require analytical thinking and strategic adaptability alongside technical proficiency.
items.title: LPT Skills Adapts Digital Marketing Curriculum for AI Era

items.summary: A Mexican judge sentenced three men to 158 years and nine months each for murdering Australian brothers Jake and Callum Robinson and US friend Carter Rhoad. The killings occurred during a surfing trip in Baja California in 2024 following an apparent botched robbery. The victims' bodies were discovered a week later. The girlfriend of the alleged ringleader received a separate 20-year sentence for admitting involvement in the robbery.
items.title: Three Men Sentenced to 158 Years for Murdering Surfers in Mexico

items.summary: California Highway Patrol officials reported a Tesla crashed into a patrol vehicle on Interstate 80 while the driver was allegedly asleep with Full Self-Driving active. Two officers were seriously injured. The department clarified that Full Self-Driving is not fully autonomous and requires continuous driver supervision, warning that distracted driving remains dangerous even with advanced technology.
items.title: Tesla Driver Allegedly Asleep While Using Full Self-Driving System

items.summary: Anthropic published a report indicating significant changes in its workforce composition and operations over the past year. The company notes a decrease in junior-level hires and a reduction in technical teams' share of the workforce. Additionally, meeting time per employee has increased by 20%, attributed to the need for human trust and accountability in an AI-integrated environment.
items.title: Anthropic Reports Workforce Shifts and Increased Meeting Time

items.summary: Replit CEO Amjad Masad stated that the company is no longer working with Anthropic, citing cost and performance reasons. However, insiders and website evidence suggest the partnership remains active, with Anthropic models still accessible.
